newsitem.title: SPAIN: RALLYING-LIATTI TAKES LEAD IN CATALUNYA RALLY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-LIATTI TAKES LEAD IN CATALUNYA RALLY.

text.p: Italian Piero Liatti took the lead in the Catalunya Rally on Tuesday as a thrilling three-way battle developed between the Subaru driver, his British team-mate Colin McRae and Finnish reigning world champion Tommi Makinen.
Liatti ended the 10th stage, at La Figuera, just two seconds ahead of McRae, having begun the second day just one second behind the overnight leader.
Makinen, who started the day 12 seconds off the lead, closed in during the day's first four stages to lie just one second adrift of McRae.
As the leaders continued their untroubled run back to the coastal base of Lloret de Mar, behind them the Ford team of Spaniard Carlos Sainz and German Armin Schwarz suffered problems.

Local hero Sainz, who suffered a puncture earlier in the day, was beginning to drop back from the leading three drivers when he lost five minutes on the 10th stage with a broken propshaft that ended his challenge for a podium finish.

His team-mate Schwarz had been the only championship contender to finish the first four rounds of the season, but his luck ran out on the seventh stage when his car filled with smoke from a split silencer box.
The heat from the exhaust then broke his propshaft on the following Prades run, although he was able to reach the next service point for urgent repairs.
But Schwarz retired for good on the ninth stage, although the team were not sure whether the problem was related to the earlier propshaft failure.

The problems for the Ford team left Italian Angelo Medeghina in fourth place at the head of another tightly-fought battle. The Subaru driver was just one second ahead of Spaniard Jaime Azcona in the Peugeot and four seconds clear of Frenchman Gilles Panizzi in the Peugeot.
Tuesday's remaining three stages will take the teams back to Lloret de Mar for an overnight stop before the final leg begins early on Wednesday morning.
